answers.module_purpose: Bloomberg-style matter command center chrome: sidebar, › command line, command palette, status bar, and split workspace wrapping Matter Home and mnemonic routes. Chat is a module at /chat, not the landing page. One high-conflict Michigan custody matter. Primary operator is a self-represented litigant (not a lawyer). Agno is evidence truth; this app never clones evidence.
answers.user_role: Self-represented litigant (Michigan family court / Genesee 7th Circuit). Not a lawyer. Must remain usable at expert density.
answers.tech_stack: Next.js 16.3 App Router + React 19.2 + TypeScript. No Vite. cmdk already installed. Tailwind 4 + shadcn cited in CAT2 but not yet installed. FastAPI legal-api sibling on :8010.
answers.aesthetic_direction: Bloomberg terminal / legal-terminal-master dark graphite, concealed complexity, IBM Plex Mono + Inter + Playfair Display (self-hosted OFL). Progressive disclosure: keep the density, put a plain-English layer on top.
answers.data_viz_needs: Combination: dense tables + AI chat/agent panel + database/source explorer + matter-document-party relationships + status/ingestion chrome. Keyboard-first command bar.
answers.must_haves: WCAG 2.2 AA; keyboard-first; self-hosted fonts only (no Google CDN); MIT/Apache/OFL licenses; keep existing CSS tokens in globals.css; Confidential Mode persist + no consumer-model fallback; CHAT is /chat not landing; never clone Agno evidence; no Vite; no TUI; export tables as CSV/JSON later; cmdk already in tree; every mnemonic has a plain-English name + one-line Michigan explanation; do not Barney-down — treat the user as a capable adult who is not a lawyer.

library.name: Existing graphite CSS tokens + cmdk; adopt shadcn/ui + Tailwind 4 incrementally
library.why: CAT2 already locked Next 16 + shadcn + Tailwind 4. The running app already has legal-terminal-master tokens, cmdk, and a working shell. A big-bang Tailwind preflight rewrite would trash that. termcn is an Ink TUI (CAT2: no TUI). Blueprint v6 is React-19-ready but Sass/CSS-in-JS and fights the existing token file. Fortress is a paid finance template, not a library.

rejected.name: termcn (shadcn-labs/termcn)
rejected.why: Ink + OpenTUI. CLI/TUI only. CAT2 forbids a TUI for this app.

rejected.name: Palantir Blueprint v6
rejected.why: Excellent dense tables (Apache-2.0, React 19 as of v6.16, 2026-06-09). Wrong styling engine for a Tailwind-bound Next app that already has graphite tokens.

rejected.name: Fortress / glitchcn / cyberpunk kits
rejected.why: Paid template or neon scanlines. Wrong license posture and wrong legal aesthetic.

rejected.name: Classic amber-on-black Bloomberg clone
rejected.why: Nostalgic, worse for long legal reading. Confidential gold already occupies amber. Keep graphite.

library.install_later: When the next primitive is needed (Tooltip, Dialog, DataTable): npm i tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss; import utilities only (no preflight); npx shadcn@latest add tooltip dialog. Map shadcn CSS vars onto the existing --bg/--text/--accent tokens.

color_scheme.name: Legal-terminal graphite (already in globals.css)
color_scheme.direction: Keep current tokens. Do not switch to slate/navy SaaS or amber-on-black.
rules: Never use color alone for status — pair with a word.
Amber/gold is Confidential Mode, not 'warning' unless labeled.
No pure #000 background, no pure #fff text.

layout.pattern: Persistent left sidebar + › command line + module header + split workspace + status bar
layout.keyboard: › line, Tab complete, Ctrl/Cmd+K palette, Ctrl+\ split, Esc closes split

srl_layer.audience: Michigan self-represented litigant, Genesee County / 7th Circuit, high-conflict custody. Capable adult, not a lawyer. Do not Barney-down.
srl_layer.rule: Same screen stays dense. Every control also has a plain-English name and a one-line 'what this is' explanation. Legal terms stay; they get a gloss, they are not deleted.
srl_layer.advanced_disclosure: STRAT / TEAM / AGNT / PRIV start folded under Advanced. One click opens them. Never deleted.
srl_layer.not_court_safe: Always visible as: 'Workbench only — do not file this screen with the court.'

examples.FCTR: Best-interest factors — the 12 things a Michigan judge must weigh (MCL 722.23).
examples.FOC: Friend of the Court — the county office that investigates custody and support.
examples.RELS: Release candidate — the version you review before anything is treated as ready to file.
examples.PRIV: Privilege first-pass — flags attorney-client / work-product text. Not a legal conclusion.
examples.CONF: Confidential mode — blocks consumer AI (ChatGPT/Claude). Stays on until you turn it off.
